body:
P2-25 DESIGN, part 5: tests first, and what is not recoverable (docs/tasks/P2-songs-as-references.md, parts 9, 12, 13).

TESTS FIRST. Slice 1: tests/test_textnorm.py (none exists today: grep -rl textnorm tests finds only test_lean.py, which is why nothing noticed B-37) and app/test/domain/text_fold_test.dart over the SAME app/test/fixtures/text/fold-cases.json (the server workflow lists the folder, docs/30 section I). ROWS: Arabic with and without harakat, each alef form, yeh and keheh variants, tatweel, Arabic-Indic and Persian digits; Russian with and without a stress mark, moy differs from moi, yo meets ye; a Persian title with the half-space meets the one with a plain space; Greek tonos and final sigma; Korean; Japanese voiced kana (ga differs from ka) and halfwidth katakana; Chinese; Hindi and Thai (marks kept); Hebrew niqqud; fullwidth Latin. ACCEPTANCE: two different songs give two different keys, and the same song with and without decoration meets, in FOUR shapes: (1) fully non-Latin; (2) MIXED SCRIPT: a Latin artist with two Arabic, Cyrillic or Japanese titles that start the same; an Arabic artist and the same Latin title for two artists; YOASOBI with two Japanese titles; two Japanese artists with the title First Love; Kino and Lyube with a Latin title; (3) EXTENDED LATIN: Polish, Turkish, Vietnamese, German, Icelandic, Scandinavian (Lukasz with the l-stroke meets Lukasz and differs from Ukasz; Strasse meets the sharp-s spelling; Thorunn meets the thorn spelling; Nguyen meets the stacked-mark spelling; Simarik meets the dotless-i spelling); (4) TYPOGRAPHIC (a curly apostrophe meets a straight one; an en dash is two words). PROPERTIES: ASCII input keeps today's word list (20,000 seeded strings); idempotent over every code point; no letter or digit gives an empty key; a corpus test fails when a Python or Unicode upgrade changes any result ("bump TEXTNORM_REVISION"). SLICE 2: facts_to_fill does not copy a basis between two Arabic artists (fails today); pick_song and find_existing find an Arabic title and keep two apart; one Deezer hit for two Arabic songs matches neither wrongly; rank accepts an exact Arabic result and refuses a one-syllable-off Hangul title; the janitor retires a ref kept alive only by an old-revision not_found. SLICE 3 on a database built with the frozen old fold (tests/legacy_fold.py, test code only): keys new, counts of likes, entries, plays, ref_merge and ref_gone unchanged, idempotent, a failed rewrite changes nothing and starts the server, refmerge holds a pair with a worklist ref. SLICE 4 with the fake music server of test_scanner.py: seven tagged files (3 Fairuz Arabic, 2 Kino Russian, 2 Radiohead) linked with the OLD fold then repaired give seven songs; the original ref keeps its likes; an ISRC match keeps the file; a keeper file never moves; a second pass moves nothing; an incomplete pass keeps the worklist; a library-source file is only ever re-pointed (the disk is untouched; rehome.py imports nothing that writes to the music folder); the feed returns both refs; the phone test of a split page (a new ref inserted, an audio key changed, nothing dropped).

NOT RECOVERABLE (say it plainly to the Host): (1) songs only streamed: a like, entry, play or queue position made on a song the server showed as A while meant as B is a row on A, and the server never stored what was meant; (2) plays and Year in Music of A may hold B audio; (3) a merge by file made while the key was empty is never undone; (4) songs of a playlist import: import.url and import_entry.video name the song the source meant, but only until PR #94 purges the entries (60 days after the import, 90 for removed playlist entries), and changing a person list is not automatic (refmerge holds same_playlist for the same reason); (5) Navidrome stars: bring-my-library-over adds likes for the now separate songs; a playlist it filled once is not refilled (N-37).
